module_mood_contract: curious readiness — 'I've built enough to try; let's see what the agent does.' (Module 4, run-the-first-experiment.md — Meta target block). This lecture is the M4-open map-reveal container, wired into '## Start here' after the Connections task-pick and before The agent loop / Test and learn / walk-and-send-off.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Placement diagnostic: this is a ceiling-reveal opener, not a meta-frame closer. It sits at M4's open before any exercise and shows the map's far side ('Verification, Absorption, Outcome') before the student starts the un-packaged session. The separate post-launch closer names backpressure only after that session starts.

Rule's scope is explicitly M5-style contrast-mood modules ('learn through doing the thing, name it after'). M4's mood is curious readiness, not the M5 contrast register the rule calibrates dosage against. The lecture's own maintainer block independently commits to the same spirit (3–5 min container, 'not a teaching lecture,' no packaging law named), which the trace confirms held — but the rule itself doesn't bind this module.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No cross-module sequencing in lecture bodies.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The body says only that 'the rest of the training goes there' and that laws are named later; these are module-arc beats in an arc/map lecture whose subject is the far-half transition. No numbered-module or named-file sequencing remains in the body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide/lecture headers pass the squint test AND the truth clause.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Three headers, no repeats: 'Back to the map: the far half opens' carries the permitted orientation beat; 'Long-running answers to three new governors' is supported by the three governor bullets; 'Your first un-packaged long session' truthfully names the student's send-off. No empty-container or orphan-mystery header.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A slide's BODY is size-bounded (~210 words / ≤6 bullets), not just its header.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Slide 1 (fig. excluded): 2 bullets, ~56 words. Slide 2: 4 bullets, ~188 words (closest to ceiling but under it). Slide 3: 3 bullets, ~86 words. All three under 210 words and ≤6 bullets.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forcing functions stay, scripted reactions go; forcing functions live in prompts, not body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: File is a pure lecture with zero fenced prompt blocks (confirmed via `node scripts/expand-md.js curriculum/lectures/the-far-half.md` — no {{prompt:}} markers, no **Prompt** fences). No forcing-function/prompt-placement question arises on this surface.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body teaches the work; trainer manages the room outside text.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No authored conversation/pause cues anywhere in the body ("discuss with," "share with your neighbor," "tell the room," "take N seconds" — none present). The closing carried question ('what makes you trust the result at the end?') is a self-reflective frame the student holds, not an authored trainer-cohort-management instruction. Trace's ambiguous_instructions flags it as ambiguous whether to answer aloud vs. hold silently — that's a UX/clarity note, not a conversation-authoring violation.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Mood contract named; module's deliberate mood honoured per beat.
rules_evaluated.evidence: M4 mood = curious readiness. Single-phase trace: phase mood_score 8, close mood_score 8 (both ≥8 floor). This beat is content-bearing (introduces Verification/Absorption/Outcome as named governors) so mood-floor applies rather than the mechanical-setup exemption; trace shows the reveal reads as orienting/anticipatory, not anxious or compliance-flavoured, matching the contract. Minor drag noted (Absorption lands abstract on first pass; unexplained loop-strand labels on the figure) keeps both scores at 8 rather than 9, not below the 8 floor.

"You are not handed the laws of this country up front. You feel where it bites first, here." — framed as not-yet-knowing, never as having-done-wrong. No blame language anywhere in the body; the un-packaged run is framed as an experiment to read, not a test to fail (consistent with the module file's own 'traces are data' framing).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The three named governors — Verification, Absorption, Outcome — are positive disciplines, not failure words. Title 'Long-running answers to three new governors' and each bullet leads with what the discipline GOVERNS ('Verification governs how you know the result is any good...'), not with a named failure mode. The felt problem ('quick feedback goes quiet') is named as context for why the disciplines matter, not as the section's lead.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strategy-fidelity — consolidates front-run check, module-to-module arc, Big Idea fidelity, mood-doesn't-resolve-early.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Front-run check: the body names no packaging law, no backpressure, no three-pattern, and no M5/M6 mechanism. Big Idea fidelity: slide 3 sends one long session off un-packaged so the student can learn from what the existing system does. Module arc: the lecture opens M4 and hands off to the agent-loop/test-and-learn/send-off sequence; the live post-launch closer later names backpressure, M5 builds and calibrates checks, and M6 composes them. Mood stays open because the lecture ends with the unanswered trust question.

mood_summary.teaching_moment_lands: PASS, no rule_index (per completeness contract — recorded here, not as a rules_evaluated row). Named moment: long-running work is governed by three new disciplines (Verification/Absorption/Outcome) instead of the near-half's tight feedback loop, closing on a carried question about trust. Trace shows this triggers reliably even for a persona that skims the figure's unexplained loop-strand labels — the core governor bullets and the closing question stand on their own regardless of how closely the figure is read. Minor fragility (not blocking): Absorption's definition is the most abstract of the three and needs a beat to land; a less-attentive reader could let it wash past without the Verification/Outcome anchor it lacks.
